amendments.reason: Phase 1 measured the early-exit network at n_in = 194 under the G3 timing protocol (13.754 / 20.224 / 27.143 us on cpu-1t-pcore). Training a 128-input network would mean charging it a latency measured for a different network.  The input must be the one that was timed, or the timing must be redone; keeping 194 keeps Phase 1's frozen charges applicable verbatim, and the extra features are free at the same shape.

amendments.reason: Found on the VALIDATION city, which is the split designated for model selection; no test city informed it.  Three defects, all in the predictor rather than in the controller: (1) the zero sentinel made 'not measured' indistinguishable from 'measured at 0 dB', which is inside the informative range; (2) the controller probes up to 64 beams but the predictor never saw more than 16 in training; (3) the final round saw only model-ordered prefixes while the fixed-K baselines feed it frozen-order ones, so the published-architecture comparison was evaluating it off its own training distribution.  Symptom: at K >= 8 the anytime predictor was WORSE than taking the best measured beam with no network at all (eta 0.477 against 0.642 at K=8), and worse than the FC and CNN comparators trained on the same data.
amendments.state_when_made: validation numbers seen; test numbers from the defective predictor were also computed and are superseded, and the superseded gate outcome is reported alongside the final one
amendments.to: unprobed beams encoded at the sentinel -40 dB (the clip floor); training probe counts uniform on 1..48; the final round trained on a 50/50 mixture of frozen-order and model-ordered prefixes

Simultaneous 95% intervals in the two versions the paper uses: (i) bootstrap, D +/- q SE*, with q the 0.95 quantile (numpy, linear) over replicates of the maximum over the family of |D* - D|/SE*; (ii) t, D +/- q_t SE_t, with SE_t = (s_seed^2/S + SE_block^2)^(1/2) as in paired_bootstrap_hier and q_t the t_(S-1) quantile at the per-comparison level 2(1 - Phi(q)) that q implies; a difference is established when both exclude zero.  Reported descriptively besides: per point-estimate change, the rate lost 1 - R2(w1)/R2(w2) with its marginal seed-by-block and t intervals, scaled by the point estimate of R2(w2), and its simultaneous lower bound; both contrasts; the candidate sets; the shares of replicates with the same change and with any change; and the replicate distribution of the number of changes among the 72 pairs

analyses.aging_bound: aging.run_site is re-run for the six evaluation scenarios at 0, 3, 30, 60 and 120 km/h with the ten seeds and the P-core latencies, exactly as aging.py's main calls it, with aging.summarize wrapped so that G(t) = ba[1] (summed over users of the largest held-beam rate over the 64 layer-6 beams, divided by their number) and r_S(t) (the seed mean of sweep64's held-beam curve) are kept on aging.py's grid, t_p/4 plus every breakpoint, before the original summarize runs.  Per (scenario, speed): the shortfall int_{d_S}^{T_max} (G - r_S) and the slack, the least d_L - d_S with int_{d_S}^{d_L} G >= that shortfall, with d_S the sweep's completion time (64 t_p) and T_max = 10 ms.  Per exclusion of rules.json R5: tau - tau* at the fastest runtime, with tau* that profile's own, against the largest slack over the six scenarios at each speed

criteria.criterion: an exclusion of R5 holds under aging at a speed if its tau - tau* exceeds the largest slack over the six scenarios at that speed.  The slack is computed at the P-core per-probe time, the aging simulation's; the other profiles' per-probe times differ from it by at most 0.63 us, and the paper states the margin by which each exclusion clears the slack

analyses.rerank_charge: c_rank = the sweep_select charge of lat_cpu1t_pcore.json, a masked argmax over 64 entries timed by the stage-4 protocol: 1.060 us.  sim.elapsed_us adds c_rank * k * 1[i >= 1] to d(i, k) = k t_p + tau_i + (k + i + 1) c_lookup, charging every probe of a decision sequence that has invoked the predictor, those before the first call included: an overcharge that keeps d a function of (i, k), so one backward-induction pass per T stays exact and the table's shape and its timed lookup (0.296 us) are unchanged.  It applies in the planner (solve, solve_blinkered, solve_osla: the variants dp, osla, blind, one, blnk, rep1, deep1) and in the executor (methods.scheduled when reorder is true); dpn, anyr, fcc and cnnc never re-rank and noc never infers, so they are charged nothing.  The latency-unaware planner is given c_rank, like every other non-inference charge, so aware against unaware still isolates the awareness of tau.  c_rank is not scaled by rho (it is controller logic, like the lookup and the per-probe processing) and is zero under airtime-only accounting.  evaluate.check_charge asserts that the planner and the executor charge the same c_rank

analyses.zhang_np2: methods.zhang_np2_descent and zhang_np2, Zhang et al.'s Algorithms 1-2 and eqs. (13)-(17), (24) in this measurement model, as variant 'zhang-NP2'.  Per receiver and layer k = 1..6 the two children of the previous winner are trained.  Look 1 is the raw statistic behind y (sim.measure_chi2: measure()'s draws before the floor and the clip; the receiver detects); looks 2.. are (Z + sqrt(lam))^2 + Q from an array drawn once per (scenario, seed) by default_rng(stable_seed(name, seed, 'zf')), Z standard normal and Q chi-square(31), shape (users, 126, 4), indexed (receiver, codeword, look - 2): common to every T and every variant, and independent of y, gen and gen2.  After each look, the log-likelihood ratio of the running energy sum, H0 noise only and H1 a single Rayleigh path of known variance sigma_a^2 in the codeword's sector (gain C_k = 2^(k-1), Zhang's -3 dB rule): ln LR = -ln(1 + n m) + ln 1F1(1; 16 n; S n m / (2(1 + n m))), m = 16 P sigma_a^2 C_k / sigma_p^2; H1 at ln LR >= ln 4.75, H0 at ln LR <= ln 0.0625 (Pa = 0.2, Pm = 0.05), otherwise another look, at most 3.  The child with the larger mean energy wins whatever the test decided (Algorithm 2).  A codeword costs t_p for its first look (pilot, feedback and the per-probe processing) and 10 us of pilot for each further look (Zhang's per-pair T_E + T_f: one feedback), plus C_DEC = 0.142 us per look and per layer, which undercharges the likelihood test.  The layer rule looks back: R_k = (1 - D_k/T)+ G_k with G_k eq. (24)'s expected rate given the first look's detection threshold, stopping at the first k where R_k > R_(k-1) and k < 6 fails and outputting layer k.  sigma_a^2 is each receiver's own mean channel power over the 64 DFT beams, which favours the baseline; there is no budget rule, as in the paper, so a descent that overruns T delivers nothing and its share is recorded.  Its contrasts with sched-pi and sched are added to evaluate.py's mechanism pairs, keyed by pair

analyses.description: two changes to the experiment, declared before they run.  (1) The controller's choice of the next codeword after an inference call, a masked argmax over the exit's 64 output scores on every probe, was in no timed component and so charged nowhere; it is charged from now on, in the planner and the executor, and every controller result is re-solved and re-evaluated with it.  (2) The adaptive baseline was a simplified reimplementation of Zhang et al.; their algorithm as published is added beside it.  No model is retrained and nothing is timed; every output carries the suffix _rr, and no recorded file is written

analyses.guarded_baselines: methods.zhang_guarded (the reimplementation, AHTBS+AHIBS form) and methods.zhang_np2_guarded (the published descent), reported as zhang-G and zhang-NP2-G beside the unguarded forms.  Before every look the elapsed time plus that look, the check and the layer decision that may follow must stay below T, the controller's own feasibility rule; a check costs c_guard = 0.142 us (np_test, a threshold comparison; 0 under airtime-only accounting) whether it passes or not.  The first look that cannot fit ends the descent (no later look is cheaper); a test the guard cuts short keeps its looks; a layer is complete when both children have a first look, and the beam is the winner of the deepest complete layer (none, and zero rate, if layer 1 is incomplete).  The detection tests, the hierarchy and the layer rules are each form's own.  Common random numbers: the published form runs on the same first looks and repeat arrays; the reimplementation's guarded call draws its repeats from a generator set to gen2's state just before the unguarded call at the same T, drawing every look slot for every user in the same order, so its draws are a prefix of the unguarded call's, and gen2's own stream is untouched.  The unguarded reimplementation's overrun share is recorded beside it.  Contrasts sched-pi and sched against each guarded form join evaluate.py's mechanism pairs, keyed by pair

T starts at the slot whose DCI triggers the set and its report.  The sweep measures 64 resources and the candidate K = 4; the report, its delay and the gNB's processing are common to both, so they cancel in d_L - d_S and, entering d_S, only shrink the allowance: the verdicts take them as zero, which is conservative. analyses.proposition_1d: Proposition 1, part (d), a random completion time.  Let the method select among the M beams, let its completion time D_L be random and independent of the channel, let T_max > d_S and psi(T) = E[(T - D_L)^+] - eta_S (T - d_S)^+.  It outperforms the sweep in expected rate at T only if psi(T) > 0, and a perfect predictor does exactly then.  If psi(T_max) <= 0, those periods form one interval (ess inf D_L, a) with a <= T_max, empty when D_L >= d_S almost surely; the condition then reads E[min(D_L, T_max)] >= eta_S d_S + (1 - eta_S) T_max, part (a) at the mean of the completion time capped at T_max.  Lower bounds on eta_S and on D_L and an upper bound on d_S, which D_L must then exceed, may replace them.  Proof: in each realization the selected beam's rate is at most the best beam's, and D_L is independent of the latter, so E[R_L(T)] <= (G/T) E[(T - D_L)^+], with equality for a perfect predictor; E[(T - D_L)^+] is convex and nondecreasing in T and positive exactly above ess inf D_L; the sweep delivers nothing below d_S; on [d_S, T_max] psi is convex, so psi(a) <= 0 and psi(T_max) <= 0 give psi <= 0 on [a, T_max]; psi(T_max) = T_max - E[min(D_L, T_max)] - eta_S (T_max - d_S); the bounds only raise psi; a deterministic D_L recovers part (a).  A fixed percentile of D_L is therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for an exclusion in expected rate
analyses.trace_decisive: One process per case and run, sequential, never concurrent, interleaved run 1 A B C, run 2 A B C, run 3 A B C.  Pinning and environment as run_all.sh: taskset -c 0-15 (the eight P-cores with SMT); case A with eight threads (OMP, OpenBLAS and MKL at 8, torch.set_num_threads(8)) and no CUDA device visible; cases B and C with one thread and torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), cudnn.benchmark on; gradients off; warnings silenced as run_all.sh did, those raised while building recorded.  Runtimes: uncompiled, calibrate.build (the stored eager closures: the network and argmax, then torch.cuda.synchronize on the GPU), and TorchScript of the whole decision, calibrate_opt2.build (traced, frozen, optimize_for_inference), so the networks, weights (seeds 17, 29, 43), inputs and freezing are the stored campaign's.  Boundaries: 'host', the closure's result converted by int() inside the timed call, which on the GPU copies the index from device memory, the boundary of record; 'device', the index left in device memory as the stored GPU timings left it, for case C only, to measure the copy.  Case A: uncompiled and TorchScript at the host boundary (TorchScript on eight threads was never timed before); B: the same; C: both runtimes at both boundaries.  Per configuration and seed: 1,000 warm-up and 10,000 timed calls (the protocol's full counts; calibrate.timed, time.perf_counter_ns around each call), then the recheck with a quarter of each (250 and 2,500); drift = |recheck p95 - p95| / p95, the nearest-rank 95th percentile of calibrate.nearest_rank_p95.  Before timing, each process waits for a quiet machine: ten samples over 5 s, each with GPU utilization at most 10% and a one-minute load average at most 1.0, polled every 30 s for up to 60 min; if it never comes, the process writes r<run>_<case>_notstarted.json and the campaign stops.  The machine's state (load, governor, energy preference, turbo, the pinned CPUs' frequencies, the GPU's utilization, clocks, temperature, power, performance state and processes, the busiest CPU processes) is read from /proc, sysfs, nvidia-smi and ps before and after every configuration, never during one; calibrate.env_record once, after the last.  A configuration is contended if its drift exceeds 10% for any seed, and a process with a contended configuration is repeated once, immediately, as attempt 2; every attempt is kept.  Outputs, written once: trace_decisive/r<run>_<case>[_a2].json, per seed the counts, median, mean, quartiles, 95th and 99th percentiles, minimum, maximum, the recheck's 95th percentile, drift and lag-one autocorrelation, with the state and environment; and the .npz beside it, every timed and recheck call in nanoseconds in call order.  --smoke DIR runs every configuration with 3 warm-up and 10 timed calls (recheck 1 and 3) into a directory outside the outputs, without the declaration gate and without waiting for a quiet machine

R19.text: R12, R14 and R16 read levels.json's tests at nrtime.py's threshold for the paper's procedure, 12 resources per slot with a 120 kHz control carrier at the declarable timing most favourable to ResNet-18 on the GPU (0.9393066873786408), exactly as they read csirs.json's and csirs_cfg.json's at csirs.py's 0.9496991264367816, which it supersedes. R20.note: set after the stored calls had been examined, before the repeated runs
R20.text: (i) The stored timings remain the inputs of Table I, of rule R5's verdicts, of every margin and of every number computed from them; the campaign is reported beside them and replaces none.  Table I's rows keep their stored categories; a row whose controlled reading below differs carries a mark, and the text gives that reading.  (ii) In each uncontended run (an attempt none of whose configurations drifted by more than 10% for any seed; an uncontended second attempt counts as its run) and at each boundary, a case is read as R5 and Table I read it, at its fastest runtime's charge, that runtime's largest per-seed 95th percentile in the run: excluded at the measured inputs if 4 t_p + charge >= (1 - eta) T_max + eta 64 t_p, with eta = 0.9993, the lowest measured sweep efficiency, t_p the profile's own per-probe time and T_max = 10 ms; and at adverse inputs if 4 x 20 us + tau_lo >= (1 - eta_lo) T_max + eta_lo d_S_hi, with eta_lo = 0.972181695575957 and d_S_hi = 1341.824 us (margins.json) and tau_lo the smallest per-seed 95th percentile over the run's runtimes at that boundary, a point value.  Each runtime's reading is reported as well, descriptively.  (iii) A case's verdict is stable if, at both sets of inputs, the stored timing and every uncontended run at the host boundary give the same; otherwise it is called unresolved, and the paper names the runs, runtimes or boundary that disagree.  A case with fewer than two uncontended runs has no controlled verdict.  (iv) For case C the paper also reports, per run at the host boundary, the CSI-RS threshold at the fastest runtime's charge (nrtime.worst, 12 resources per slot, a 120 kHz control carrier), the margin at adverse inputs at density 3's declared bound computed as for the stored timing, and, by part (d), the threshold at the mean of min(D*, T_max), D* = s_L - 125 us + tau per call, with D* >= s_S checked on every call; the stored CSI-RS reading is unchanged.  (v) Part (d) is read per case, run, runtime and boundary on D = 4 t_p + tau, one per recorded call: the share of D below 64 t_p and of D_lo = 4 x 20 us + tau below d_S_hi; psi(T_max) = T_max - m - eta (T_max - 64 t_p) at the measured inputs, m the smallest per-seed mean of min(D, T_max); and psi_lo(T_max) = T_max - m_lo - eta_lo (T_max - d_S_hi) at adverse inputs, m_lo the smallest per-seed one-sided 95% lower bound on the mean of min(D_lo, T_max) by batch means (batches of 100 consecutive calls, t with 99 degrees of freedom).  'Excluded in expected rate for every T up to T_max' is stated for a case only if, in every uncontended run, runtime and boundary, every recorded D_lo is at least d_S_hi and psi_lo(T_max) <= 0; if every recorded D is at least 64 t_p but some D_lo falls below d_S_hi, it is stated at the measured inputs only; if some recorded D falls below 64 t_p, the paper gives the periods (min D, a) at which a perfect predictor with that distribution could outperform the sweep in expected rate, a the zero of psi above 64 t_p on the run's pooled calls, and the largest advantage there as a share of the genie-aided rate.  'Every recorded call' stands in for 'almost surely' and is worded so.  (vi) Nothing else is re-timed and no stored file changes.
